name: Safi al-Din al-Hilli
bio: Abd al-Aziz ibn Saraya al-Sinbisi al-Ta'i, whom al-Zirikli calls “the poet of his age”, was born in al-Hilla, between Kufa and Baghdad, in 677 AH (1278 CE). He worked as a merchant, travelling to Syria, Egypt and Mardin and coming back to Iraq. His editor Muhammad Mazloum says that he left Iraq in 701 AH (1301 CE), after the blood feud between his tribe and its rivals, and joined the Artuqid kings of Mardin, for whom he wrote the Artuqiyyat, twenty-nine poems, one on each letter of the alphabet; in 726 AH (1326 CE) he went to Cairo and praised the sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun. Besides his diwan he wrote al-Atil al-Hali, on the popular verse forms zajal and mawaliya. He died in Baghdad in 750 AH (1349 CE), though the year is disputed.
